title: Getting Started
text:
Warning



Preview install. Use the source checkout for the current review build. A package-index release has not been published, and the MLPerf EDU component license remains a release gate.
This guide takes you from an empty checkout to a functional dashboard and one quality-bearing result. A GPU is optional. PyTorch uses Apple MPS or CUDA when available and otherwise runs the supported path on CPU.

title: Getting Started
text:
Before You Begin
Use macOS, Linux, or a Linux environment such as WSL. The commands on this site use a POSIX-compatible shell. Confirm that Git and uv are available.
git --version
uv --version
MLPerf EDU supports Python 3.10 or newer. uv selects and manages the locked project environment, so a separate virtual-environment command is not needed.

title: Getting Started
text:
Run the Guided Setup
git clone https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book
cd cs249r_book/mlperf-edu
uv sync --locked
uv run mlperf init --profile min --output-dir submissions/first-run
init performs the shortest complete product journey. It checks Python, PyTorch, the available device, caches, and the registry. It then runs the four-workload starter collection, verifies every provenance manifest, and writes aggregate HTML, JSON, and CSV reports. Nothing opens automatically.
The output directory should contain an aggregate suite report and four sets of workload artifacts.
submissions/first-run/
├── mlperf_edu_min_<timestamp>.html
├── mlperf_edu_min_<timestamp>.json
├── mlperf_edu_min_<timestamp>.csv
├── image-classification_min_report.*
├── causal-language-modeling_training_min_report.*
├── graph-node-classification_min_report.*
├── time-series-forecasting_min_report.*
└── *.provd.json
The terminal prints the exact report paths. Open the generated HTML file directly when you want to inspect it. Routine setup and validation never open a browser automatically.

title: Getting Started
text:
Understand the Three Setup Commands








Command
What It Does
When to Use It




mlperf doctor
Inspects the environment and selected workload prerequisites without running a benchmark
Diagnose setup or preflight a specific workload


mlperf init
Runs doctor, the four-workload starter smoke path, provenance verification, and reporting
First contact with the project


mlperf health
Runs and verifies all fourteen functional min paths and writes a suite health dashboard
Validate a course image or the full local installation



Do not run all three during initial setup. init is the canonical first step. Use doctor when something fails and health when you need complete functional coverage.

title: Getting Started
text:
Read the First Dashboard
The min dashboard answers whether the selected paths executed and whether their manifests verified. It does not compare functional diagnostics with quality targets. Read the report in this order.

Confirm that every selected path executed.
Confirm that provenance verification passed.
Check the actual device and configuration used.
Treat secondary metrics as diagnostics, not benchmark scores.

The results guide explains every dashboard state and the claims each state supports.

title: Getting Started
text:
Run the First Quality Contract
Image classification is the recommended first max workload because it has a small, bounded accuracy set and a direct target. Preview the contract and asset work before downloading or measuring.
uv run mlperf show image-classification
uv run mlperf fetch --workload image-classification --profile max --dry-run
uv run mlperf fetch --workload image-classification --profile max
uv run mlperf run --workload image-classification --profile max \
  --output-dir submissions/image-max
The run writes HTML, JSON, CSV, and .provd.json files without opening them. The HTML lead card reports top-1 accuracy, the target of at least 0.85, and the pass or miss decision. Verify the recorded bytes after the run.
uv run mlperf verify submissions/image-max/image-classification_max.provd.json

title: Getting Started
text:
Know What Success Means
Execution success, provenance verification, and target attainment are separate states. A valid run may miss its quality target. That is a scientific result, not an execution failure. A missing dataset, crashed runner, or invalid manifest is an execution problem and does not support a quality conclusion.
Continue with the running guide for selection and profiles, the results guide for interpretation, or troubleshooting if setup did not complete.

title: Getting Started
text:
Contributor Setup
The development tools are not required for normal benchmark use. Contributors can install them after the student journey works.
uv sync --locked --extra dev
uv run python -m pytest

title: Instructors and Maintainers
text: Students begin with init and health, then use fetch, run, and report for selected benchmark work. Everything else on this page validates the suite itself or verifies what students submit.

title: Instructors and Maintainers
text:
Auditing the Registry Contract
uv run mlperf audit --policy public  # expected status 1 while the portfolio is experimental
The nonzero audit status is an expected policy block for this review draft, not a workload execution failure.
audit inspects registry metadata without running anything. It checks that score-bearing workloads declare complete quality targets, that datasets and models carry source and license information, and that public statuses are internally consistent. Run it after any registry edit.

title: Instructors and Maintainers
text:
Validation Presets
uv run mlperf validate smoke                 # fast end-to-end functional check
uv run mlperf validate coverage              # every registered min path
uv run mlperf validate max                   # every registered max path
uv run mlperf validate release --output-dir submissions/validation
Presets execute workloads and grade the artifacts they produce. smoke runs on each change. Actual max and release execution runs through the scheduled or manually dispatched release workflow. Selection-only dry runs do not count as benchmark evidence.
mlperf health is the student-facing wrapper around the coverage preset. It checks the actual all-workload selection, keeps enough partial evidence to diagnose failures, and writes the suite health report without opening a browser.

title: Instructors and Maintainers
text:
Grading Student Submissions
uv run mlperf grade submissions --output submissions/grade.json
uv run mlperf grade submission.zip \
  --assignment examples/05-assignment-package/assignment.yaml \
  --output submission-grade.json
grade accepts a directory, one .provd.json manifest, or one portable ZIP package. It verifies provenance and recorded quality-target satisfaction before emitting a machine-readable grade file. A versioned assignment YAML can also fix the expected workload, profile, mode, phase, result count, quality decision, and configuration subset. Portable packages are inspected and extracted with a fail-closed path and integrity policy. Unknown assignment fields are rejected, and the grade records the SHA-256 of the exact assignment contract. For every quality-bearing result, grading also requires the registry metric, target, direction, and tolerance and recomputes the decision from the observed value. Instructors should still rerun selected submissions when course policy requires behavioral or performance verification.

title: Instructors and Maintainers
text:
Course Integration Pattern
Keep canonical benchmark artifacts and classroom experiments distinct. Students can run a registered reference workload (uv run mlperf run --workload X --profile max), inspect its report, and submit the verified result directory or manifest under the applicable course policy. Portable packages are suitable only when the asset policy permits them. The CLI intentionally refuses packages that would include fetch-only or release-review dataset bytes. Example 05 uses an image-classification min result for the portable packaging exercise and makes no quality claim.
The default dashboard makes this sequence visible. Students should first interpret the readiness or quality lead view, then confirm configuration and checkpoint lineage, and finally verify the provenance manifest. A min dashboard is evidence that the setup works, not that the benchmark target was met.
The three Python files under examples/ are standalone teaching experiments. Labs 1 and 3 run their own training comparisons. Lab 2 implements SUT_Interface and drives it locally, but the product CLI has no generic --sut plugin-loading option. Lab output must not be presented as a canonical benchmark artifact. The assignment package example shows a portable functional artifact and contract-grading path without redistributing a score-bearing dataset. Examples 2 and 3 carry the authoritative quality work.
The numbered classroom sequence covers suite health, a controlled inference tradeoff, training-to-inference lineage, compatibility-checked result comparison, and portable assignment grading. Every example includes allowed changes, interpretation questions, and a suggested ten-point rubric. Instructors should trial the selected workloads on the course image and publish their own time budgets before assigning them. Examples 2 and 3 use --reference-plan to compare a student’s normalized plan with the instructor copy before execution. The edit policy belongs to the instructor reference, permits only named candidate environment settings, and cannot authorize changes to a baseline or undeclared variable. The aggregate report and provenance bind both plan files and record every accepted edit.
For long training labs, a schema 0.3 plan can attach a baseline_import to its baseline run. The plan records a relative .provd.json path and exact manifest SHA-256. Before accepting it, the runner verifies the manifest and source report, canonical quality decision, baseline role, workload, mode, phase, device, and every declared configuration setting. The aggregate uses a new wrapper manifest and leaves the instructor’s original result unchanged. A candidate-only student execution therefore retains a reviewable baseline without presenting copied numbers as a fresh run.

title: Instructors and Maintainers
text:
Keeping the Docs Honest
Benchmark pages on this site are generated from the registry:
uv run python tools/generate_docs.py           # regenerate after registry edits
uv run python tools/generate_docs.py --check   # CI gate that fails on drift
If you change a workload YAML and the site, the --check gate fails until the pages are regenerated, so documentation and harness cannot disagree.

title: Lab 2 SUT Interface
text:
MLPerf EDU includes an educational mlperf.sut.SUT_Interface, but its current integration is deliberately narrow. Lab 2 is the only shipped lab that implements this interface. It constructs the SUT directly and drives it from the lab script so students can compare naïve and KV-cache decoding while checking token-for-token output parity.
The supported product command, uv run mlperf run, dispatches workloads that are registered in the repository. It does not expose a generic --sut option and does not discover or load arbitrary student plugin files. A Lab 2 result is therefore a standalone classroom experiment, not a canonical MLPerf EDU result or a plugin submission accepted by the product CLI.

title: Lab 2 SUT Interface
text:
The Interface Used by Lab 2
Lab 2 defines a class that inherits mlperf.sut.SUT_Interface and implements the interface’s constructor and asynchronous query method:
from mlperf.sut import SUT_Interface

class StudentNanoGPTSUT(SUT_Interface):
    def __init__(self, config):
        # load the lab model and prepare its execution device
        ...

    async def process_queries(self, samples):
        # run the selected decode implementation and return measurements
        ...
The lab creates deterministic QuerySample inputs, calls process_queries locally, and records latency, throughput, and output-parity evidence. This is a useful teaching seam, but it is not wired into the generated benchmark runner or release-validation path.

text:
Producing Canonical Artifacts
Use registered workload commands when you need reports and provenance that the benchmark validation tools understand. For the inference path closest to Lab 2:
OUTPUT_DIR="submissions/causal-language-modeling-max"
uv run mlperf fetch --workload causal-language-modeling --mode training --profile max

The candidate public-result contract distinguishes score-bearing, performance-bearing, and systems-only workloads. See PUBLIC_RULES.md and run uv run mlperf audit --policy public before treating a registered result as a public candidate.

title: Results, Provenance, and Packaging
text: A benchmark that cannot be reviewed is a demo. MLPerf EDU treats the artifacts of a run as first-class products, designed to be handed to an instructor, an artifact evaluation committee, or a co-author.

title: Results, Provenance, and Packaging
text:
First Result Walkthrough
Begin with the lead card, then move from execution evidence to claim evidence. The first five checks prevent a fast number or green setup state from being mistaken for a valid benchmark conclusion.








Check
What to Find
What It Means




Execution
Completed or failed paths
Whether the runner produced an evaluable result


Quality
Observed metric, direction, target, and pass or miss
Whether the declared quality contract was evaluated and met


Configuration
Workload, profile, mode, phase, device, seed, and controlled settings
Which experiment the result actually represents


Lineage
Dataset revision, model source, training checkpoint, and inference dependency
Which inputs produced the observation


Provenance
Manifest state, hashes, and run fingerprint
Whether the recorded artifacts still match their manifest



A min report normally stops after functional execution and provenance. A quality-bearing max or pro report can continue through target evaluation. A target miss may still be a valid result. An execution failure or invalid manifest cannot support a quality conclusion.
The evidence states form a claim ladder.
executed → provenance verified → quality evaluated → target met or missed
         → comparison eligible → repeatability established → publication eligible
The current milestone accepts one complete run for initial quality evaluation. It does not skip the later repeatability, independent reproduction, and release review needed for a publication claim.

title: Results, Provenance, and Packaging
text:
The Four Artifacts
Every workload run emits four files, named after the workload and profile:







Artifact
Role




*_report.json
The complete result with metrics, environment fingerprint, asset dossiers, and quality status


*_report.html
The default dashboard with the lead result, target decision, configuration, lineage, and provenance


*_report.csv
Flat metrics for spreadsheets and plotting


*.provd.json
The provenance artifact: SHA-256 hashes of model state and assets



The .provd.json artifact binds a result to its recorded inputs and environment. For training workloads it can capture the frozen model state_dict hash. Inference workloads can declare and verify a shared checkpoint dependency. Verification proves that the recorded files match the manifest; it does not by itself establish benchmark validity or MLCommons acceptance.

title: Results, Provenance, and Packaging
text:
Reading the Dashboard
The lead view is derived from the report rather than a fixed profile layout. A functional-only report shows a readiness meter, passed or failed paths, and clearly secondary diagnostic values. A quality-bearing report shows target decisions and a direction-aware attainment bar where 100% means the declared gate. A mixed report keeps separate readiness and quality meters so setup success cannot hide a missed quality target.
Raw benchmark values are not combined into one cross-workload chart. Accuracy, FID, loss, AUC, and pass@1 use different units and improve in different directions. The normalized target-attainment view supports valid comparison without implying that the raw metrics share a scale. Distribution charts belong to the later stability view and appear only when repeated run evidence exists.
The remaining sections preserve the context needed to interpret each result. Run Configuration records the exact mode, phase, backend, device, seed, and workload settings. Model Lineage distinguishes a locally trained checkpoint from an upstream pretrained checkpoint and follows it through inference and evaluation. Provenance links the JSON report, manifest, run fingerprint, and checkpoint digest.
The suite health report is a second, intentionally smaller view. mlperf health runs every registered min path, verifies the manifests, and groups functional results by suite. It never places a min diagnostic beside a max quality target. Instead, each row says that quality was not evaluated and links to the detailed run artifacts.
A pro experiment-plan report adds the research question, hypothesis, declared variables, controls, exact plan hash, and a condition matrix. Each condition keeps its own quality card. The shared visualization boundary is normalized target attainment, where 100% means that condition reached its declared gate. Unrelated raw metrics never share an axis. The CSV carries the plan ID, condition name, plan hash, planned device, outer-run count, and declared environment settings for notebook analysis. When a plan labels one condition baseline and another candidate, the dashboard can show a descriptive throughput delta. That bar explains the observed one-run result; it does not bypass the standard compatibility gate or claim a stable distribution. An imported instructor baseline is labeled as imported in HTML and CSV. Its wrapper manifest binds the unchanged source report and source manifest, and its original run fingerprint remains the comparison boundary.
The aggregate provenance manifest binds the exact source plan, aggregate JSON, and every nonfailed child manifest. A missing or invalid child manifest blocks the delta and downgrades the condition to an execution failure.

title: Results, Provenance, and Packaging
text:
Reading and Converting Reports
uv run mlperf report submissions/image-max --format summary
uv run mlperf report submissions/causal-language-modeling_training_max_report.json
uv run mlperf report submissions/causal-language-modeling_training_max_report.json --format html --open
uv run mlperf report submissions/current/image-classification_max_report.json \
  --baseline submissions/baseline/image-classification_max_report.json \
  --format html --open
uv run mlperf report submissions/causal-language-modeling_training_max_report.json --format csv
uv run mlperf report submissions --format html --open                    # latest in a directory
Pointing report at a directory picks up the most recent run, which avoids copying timestamped filenames. Use a specific JSON path when a directory contains several results and the exact selection matters. HTML generation does not open a browser unless --open is present.
An explicit --baseline adds a comparison section to JSON and HTML output. The dashboard labels structurally compatible results as exploratory until both source manifests verify. Quality values are compared only when the workload, profile, mode, phase, dataset, evaluator, and target contract match. Performance bars and improvement percentages require the same checkpoint lineage and complete comparison fingerprint as well. The dashboard lists the mismatched boundary when a comparison is invalid. See the result comparison example for a compatible rerun and an intentionally blocked batch-size change.

title: Results, Provenance, and Packaging
text:
Verifying and Packaging a Submission
uv run mlperf verify submissions/causal-language-modeling_training_max.provd.json
uv run mlperf package \
  submissions/05-assignment/image-classification_min.provd.json \
  --output submissions/05-assignment.zip
verify re-checks the provenance manifest, including its hashes and recorded quality status. package bundles a verified, portable result for grading or artifact review. Many score-bearing max results bind fetch-only or release-review dataset bytes and are intentionally refused. Example 05 uses the dataset-free image-classification min path to teach portable packaging without making a quality claim. Release CI checks verification again after clean extraction.

title: Results, Provenance, and Packaging
text:
What the Fingerprint Buys You
Reports embed the hardware and software fingerprint of the machine that produced them, including Python, PyTorch, platform, and accelerator details. Matching profiles and disclosed fingerprints are necessary for comparison, but they are not sufficient. The workload, mode, phase, quality result, dataset recipe, checkpoint lineage, and release-validation state must also match.

title: 04 — Result Comparison
text:
Distinguish quality compatibility from performance compatibility and explain why the dashboard sometimes blocks a comparison instead of drawing a chart.



Use the laptop-capable image-classification workload. This example requires two authoritative runs with the same assets and device. Runtime varies by system.

  --output-dir submissions/04-comparison/baseline

  --output-dir submissions/04-comparison/current

  submissions/04-comparison/current/image-classification_max_report.json \
  --baseline submissions/04-comparison/baseline/image-classification_max_report.json \
  --format html --output submissions/04-comparison/compatible.html --open

  --output-dir submissions/04-comparison/batch-64

  --baseline submissions/04-comparison/baseline/image-classification_max_report.json \
  --format html --output submissions/04-comparison/batch-size-blocked.html --open

title: 02 — Inference Tradeoff
text:
Change one systems variable, preserve the benchmark quality contract, and explain a baseline-versus-candidate result without overstating one-run timing evidence.



The MLPerf Tiny ResNet8 workload is laptop-capable on CPU, Apple Silicon, and CUDA. The first run downloads pinned CIFAR-10 and MLPerf Tiny assets. Runtime varies by device, so instructors should trial the example on the course image.



cp examples/02-inference-tradeoff/plan.yaml student-inference-plan.yaml
# Edit only the candidate batch size in student-inference-plan.yaml.
uv run mlperf run --plan examples/02-inference-tradeoff/plan.yaml --dry-run
uv run mlperf fetch --workload image-classification --profile max
uv run mlperf run --plan student-inference-plan.yaml \
  --reference-plan examples/02-inference-tradeoff/plan.yaml
The plan runs one baseline condition and one candidate condition. Each executes the authoritative accuracy contract once and writes separate evidence under the shared experiment directory.



Students may change only the candidate batch size. The checkpoint, dataset, accuracy subset, evaluator, target, device, input representation, and baseline condition remain fixed. The plan loader rejects attempts to override the quality target.
The instructor reference declares the candidate batch-size setting as the only allowed edit. The runner compares the normalized plans before execution and rejects any baseline, device, dataset, evaluator, target, or other control change. The aggregate report and provenance bind both source files, their SHA-256 digests, and the accepted edit. If a runtime control still differs between conditions, the dashboard blocks the throughput comparison.



Read quality before throughput. Both cards should use the same top-1 accuracy target. The condition chart then shows samples per second and a descriptive candidate delta against the declared baseline. The plan hash, independent variable, controls, hardware, and condition settings explain what the bars mean.

What throughput delta did the candidate show on this machine?
Which part of the measurement changed, and which parts stayed controlled?
Why is the delta useful for a lab discussion but insufficient for a stable performance claim?

MLPERF_EDU_NCF_LEARNING_RATE and MLPERF_EDU_NCF_LR_SCHEDULE exist for one open question. The recommendation contract fixes Adam at a constant rate, HR@10 peaks early and then declines, and the upstream reference may anneal instead. Testing that requires varying the schedule without editing the contract, which is what the pro envelope is for. Both variables reject malformed or non-positive values rather than falling back to the contract, because an override that silently does nothing would make an ablation look like a null result. title: MLPerf EDU
text: MLPerf EDU connects industrial ML benchmarking rigor to single-laptop execution using zero-discretion target inheritance and fail-closed admission control across four gates: semantic (\(G_{\text{sem}}\)), protocol (\(G_{\text{protocol}}\)), provenance (\(G_{\text{provenance}}\)), and state (\(G_{\text{state}}\)). Fourteen workloads across 8 MLCommons domains share the same CLI, telemetry harness, and provenance format. Anchored in Wiggins & McTighe Backward Design, students begin with a functional min run, move to quality-bearing max contracts, and evaluate DAM Taxonomy ablations (Data, Algorithm, Machine) in controlled pro experiments.

Why It Exists
Official MLPerf suites set a high standard for benchmark governance and measurement. They are also too operationally heavy for many classroom settings. MLPerf EDU explores a smaller teaching and research layer while keeping the artifacts needed for scrutiny. The about page covers the design philosophy, independent-preview status, open licensing gates, and proposed review path.

title: Readiness
text:
Research Path
The pro profile defaults to the nine-workload research collection. An individual workload can always be selected, and --collection all expands the selection to all fourteen. Pro runs execute the max contract once by default and preserve subrun configuration and artifacts in their aggregate result.

The expected systems behavior is documented for every workload. Measured working-set, arithmetic-intensity, and dispatch classifications remain later research-characterization work and are reported as unmeasured until trace evidence exists.

title: Readiness
text:
Production Boundary
The source checkout is suitable for supervised classroom trials and bounded research evaluation. All fourteen workloads now execute locally, but this is not a production package or an accepted public benchmark. Component licensing, package publication, dataset release review, MLCommons governance, security review, independent hardware reproduction, and authenticated release artifacts remain open production gates.

title: 03 — Training Tradeoff and Checkpoint Lineage
text:
Connect a controlled training change to its checkpoint, quality decision, and downstream inference eligibility. A trained checkpoint is not acceptable merely because training finished.



This is the longest classroom example. An accelerator is recommended, and an instructor should schedule it as a take-home. Each condition performs the pinned 5,001-step NanoGPT training contract once. No five-run stability campaign is required for this milestone.
Existing Apple M5 Max evidence is roughly 34–36 minutes per training condition, or about 70 minutes for the two-condition plan before inference. This is a planning reference, not a promised runtime. Instructors should record CPU, MPS, or CUDA time, peak memory, download size, and disk use on the course image.
An instructor can run and verify the baseline once, place its report and manifest in a baseline/ directory beside the distributed student plan, and declare the relative manifest path plus its exact SHA-256 under the baseline run.
baseline_import:
  manifest: baseline/causal-language-modeling_training_pro.provd.json
  sha256: sha256:<complete-manifest-digest>
The student still submits a plan with one baseline and one candidate. The runner imports the baseline instead of executing it. It rejects a changed digest, failed provenance, a nonbaseline source condition, a target miss, or a mismatch in workload, mode, phase, device, or declared configuration. It writes a new wrapper report and manifest without modifying the instructor’s source files. This reduces the student execution budget to the candidate run while keeping the baseline visible in the aggregate dashboard.



cp examples/03-training-tradeoff/plan.yaml student-training-plan.yaml
# Edit only the candidate learning rate in student-training-plan.yaml.
uv run mlperf fetch --workload causal-language-modeling --profile max
uv run mlperf run --plan examples/03-training-tradeoff/plan.yaml --dry-run
uv run mlperf run --plan student-training-plan.yaml \
  --reference-plan examples/03-training-tradeoff/plan.yaml
The committed example executes both conditions so it works without an external baseline bundle. An instructor who distributes a precomputed baseline adds the baseline_import block to both the instructor reference and student copy before students make their permitted candidate learning-rate edit.
Run decode inference only from a condition whose training result passed the fixed validation-loss gate and whose manifest verifies.
ACCEPTED_RUN=01-baseline-lr-1e-3  # or the passing candidate directory
uv run mlperf run --workload causal-language-modeling --profile max \
  --mode inference --phase decode \
  --output-dir "submissions/03-training-tradeoff/runs/${ACCEPTED_RUN}"
The inference runner finds the training checkpoint, training report, and provenance manifest in the same directory. It refuses a failed or unverified source result.



Students may change only MLPERF_EDU_MAX_LR in the candidate. Architecture, dataset split, seed, iteration count, evaluator, and quality target remain fixed. Shortening training creates a different experiment and may cause the checkpoint to miss the unchanged gate.
The instructor reference declares the candidate learning-rate setting as the only allowed edit. The runner rejects changes to the baseline, architecture, dataset, seed, iteration count, evaluator, quality target, device, or output policy before it starts the long training run. The aggregate provenance binds both plans and records the accepted learning-rate edit.



Compare best validation loss first, then training tokens per second. Inspect the model-lineage section for the training, checkpoint, inference, and evaluation stages. The candidate result is informative even if it misses the gate, but a missed checkpoint cannot support an accepted inference result. The plan may therefore return a nonzero status after still writing useful diagnostic artifacts.

title: About MLPerf EDU
text: MLPerf EDU is an independent pedagogical ML systems benchmark preview developed alongside the Machine Learning Systems textbook. It draws methodological inspiration from MLCommons MLPerf but is not an official MLCommons benchmark and is not endorsed by MLCommons.

title: About MLPerf EDU
text:
Design Philosophy
Authoritative workload inheritance. Each score-bearing definition starts from an established upstream model, dataset split, evaluator, and quality reference. The project contributes only the PyTorch adapter, measurement harness, quality gate, provenance, and reports needed for local execution.
Traceable lineage. Workloads identify their model, dataset, scenario, runner, and research lineage. Public-result candidates add structured asset dossiers and review packets.
Introspection for teaching. The harness records systems telemetry such as arithmetic intensity, data-loading behavior, and estimated energy when the platform supports it. Students can change controlled configurations without changing the benchmark’s workload identity.
Reviewable provenance. Runs emit reports and provenance manifests that bind results to source, assets, configuration, and environment evidence. Training and inference workloads can share checkpoint lineage when the registry declares that dependency.
Canonical and classroom paths. Registered workloads produce artifacts for the benchmark validation path. The five classroom labs (Labs 1–5) provide scaffolded educational experiments anchored in Wiggins & McTighe Backward Design, advancing from basic health checks to inference trade-offs, training ablations, multi-seed comparisons, and final assignment packaging. Lab 2 demonstrates the repository’s SUT_Interface locally.

title: About MLPerf EDU
text:
Profiles as a Contract
min provides functional confidence. max runs the authoritative quality contract in its declared environment, and pro exposes the research envelope. A profile alone does not make a result publishable. Quality evidence, release validation, asset policy, and result wording must also pass the applicable gates. The running guide documents the current semantics.

title: About MLPerf EDU
text:
Single Source of Truth
Every generated benchmark page comes from the workload registry, which is also consumed by the harness. The CLI reference comes from the CLI’s own help output. CI fails when native registry files, compatibility mirrors, review packets, or generated documentation drift.

title: About MLPerf EDU
text:
Status and Governance
The repository contains the public-result rules, dataset release review, quality-target review, release checklist, and proposed MLCommons review path. The current external gates include expert target review, an authoritative component license for package publication, package-index publication, and MLCommons decisions about naming and result wording.
Development happens in the cs249r_book repository. Feedback is welcome on the issue tracker.

title: About MLPerf EDU
text:
Citing
The draft companion paper, MLPerf EDU: Bridging Industry Benchmarking and ML Systems Education, lives under paper/. It is not yet an archival benchmark citation. A stable citation will accompany a reviewed release.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Start with the narrowest command that reproduces the problem. doctor inspects the environment without running a benchmark, while health runs every functional path. Most setup problems should begin with doctor.

title: Troubleshooting
section: The Command Is Missing or Uses the Wrong Python
text:
The Command Is Missing or Uses the Wrong Python
Run commands from the mlperf-edu directory through the locked environment.
cd cs249r_book/mlperf-edu
uv sync --locked
uv run --project . python -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable)'
uv run --project . mlperf doctor
Avoid invoking a system-wide pytest, python, or mlperf executable for this checkout. Contributors should use uv run python -m pytest after installing the development extra.

title: Troubleshooting
section: A Download Is Missing or Incomplete
text:
A Download Is Missing or Incomplete
Preview the assets before downloading, then inspect the cache.
uv run mlperf fetch --workload WORKLOAD --profile max --dry-run
uv run mlperf fetch --workload WORKLOAD --profile max
uv run mlperf cache list
uv run mlperf info --dataset DATASET
The fetcher verifies pinned evidence when the source provides it. Terms-gated datasets may require a manual download and an environment-specific handoff.






Warning



Never replace a declared quality dataset with synthetic data. The runner fails closed because a synthetic substitute cannot support the same claim.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
CUDA or MPS Is Unavailable
The default --device auto policy selects CUDA, then MPS, then CPU. An explicit unavailable device fails before execution. Inspect the environment and retry on CPU when the workload supports it.
uv run mlperf doctor --workload WORKLOAD --profile PROFILE
uv run mlperf run --workload WORKLOAD --profile PROFILE --device cpu
The report records both the requested and executed device. A CPU fallback may change runtime, but it does not silently change the workload quality contract.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
The Target Was Missed
A target miss is not the same as a failed run. Check that the report shows completed execution, the declared evaluation set, the expected metric and target, and verified provenance. If those conditions hold, preserve the miss as evidence. Do not tune the threshold to match the result.
The readiness page lists four current target gaps that are being investigated without changing their published reproduction points.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Provenance Verification Failed
Verify the manifest from the unchanged result directory.
uv run mlperf verify path/to/result.provd.json
A changed model, dataset, report, or referenced file invalidates the recorded hash. Restore the exact bytes or rerun the benchmark. Do not edit a manifest to make verification pass.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Packaging Was Refused
mlperf package intentionally refuses an archive when it would include fetch-only, terms-gated, or release-review dataset bytes. Submit the verified result directory or manifest under the course policy instead. The portable packaging exercise uses the dataset-free image-classification_min artifact in Lab 5 and makes no quality claim.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
A Long Run Was Interrupted
The CLI does not yet provide a general run --resume option. Some legacy or workload-specific runners preserve their own intermediate state, but that does not create suite-wide recovery semantics. Before a long run, use fetch, run a workload-specific doctor preflight, choose an explicit output directory, and read the benchmark page for its current recovery boundary.
Do not add --resume to a command unless uv run mlperf run --help lists it. The local execution plan tracks general resumability as unfinished implementation work.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
MiniGo Cannot Start Locally
Reinforcement learning is a known local-execution blocker. Its functional min path runs, but the quality-bearing max path needs a reviewed CUDA and TensorFlow 1.x runtime on an NVIDIA system, which no laptop supplies. Inspect the machine-readable handoff instead of treating an ordinary laptop failure as a new regression.
uv run mlperf doctor --workload reinforcement-learning --profile max --format json
Recommendation is no longer in this category. It moved from DLRM on Criteo Terabyte to the MLPerf Training v0.5 NCF contract on MovieLens-20M and now trains locally in roughly half an hour. If it fails to start, treat that as a genuine problem rather than an expected blocker.

title: Troubleshooting
section: Collect a Diagnostic Bundle for a TA
text:
Collect a Diagnostic Bundle for a TA
Preserve the failing command, its terminal output, the selected workload, and the environment summary. Do not include private credentials or manually licensed dataset bytes.
uv run mlperf doctor --workload WORKLOAD --profile PROFILE --format json \
  > doctor.json
uv run mlperf run --workload WORKLOAD --profile PROFILE --dry-run \
  > selection.txt
Include the generated report and .provd.json manifest if execution reached the artifact stage. These files usually contain enough detail to distinguish an environment failure from a quality miss.

title: Research Workflows
text: The pro profile extends a workload with controlled systems conditions while preserving its identity and quality target. It is intended for bounded, single-node studies. One run is enough to test the workflow and evaluate the quality contract, but it is not stability or publication evidence.

title: Research Workflows
text:
Start With a Research Question
Use a versioned experiment plan when the study has more than one condition. The plan records the hypothesis, controlled settings, device policy, output location, and role of each condition.
uv run mlperf run --plan examples/research/pro-collection/plan.yaml --dry-run
uv run mlperf run --plan examples/research/pro-collection/plan.yaml
The dry run is the review point. Confirm the workload, dataset, mode, phase, device, baseline, candidate, and output location before any expensive work.

title: Research Workflows
text:
Compare Compatible Conditions
A plan may label one condition as baseline and another as candidate. The dashboard shows a descriptive throughput delta only when their comparison fingerprints are compatible. Quality uses normalized target attainment, where 100% means the declared gate was reached. Unrelated raw metrics never share an axis.
The included plan changes image-classification batch size while holding the quality contract fixed. It is a small example of the full research loop.

State the systems hypothesis.
Change one declared independent variable.
Keep the evaluation set, quality target, checkpoint lineage, and device policy controlled.
Inspect each condition before reading the delta.
Preserve the plan, aggregate report, child reports, and manifests together.

title: Research Workflows
text:
Interpret One-Run Evidence
A completed pro run can establish that the study design executes, the declared quality contract was evaluated, and the observed result belongs to the recorded configuration. It cannot establish a stable distribution or a publication-ready performance claim. Repetition, uncertainty analysis, independent reproduction, and release review belong to the later stability and production phases.

title: Research Workflows
text:
Preflight Expensive Work
Inspect the selected workload and assets before running it.
uv run mlperf show WORKLOAD
uv run mlperf doctor --workload WORKLOAD --profile pro
uv run mlperf fetch --workload WORKLOAD --profile pro --dry-run
uv run mlperf run --workload WORKLOAD --profile pro --dry-run
There is no general run --resume option yet. Long-running studies should use an explicit output directory and follow the recovery boundary documented on the workload page. MiniGo remains a local-execution blocker, so its page leads with preflight and handoff instructions rather than a generic laptop run.

title: Research Workflows
text:
Preserve the Review Packet
Keep the following files together for a co-author or artifact reviewer.

The exact experiment-plan YAML and its recorded SHA-256
The aggregate JSON, HTML, and CSV reports
Every condition report and .provd.json manifest
The dataset and model dossiers recorded in each report
A short interpretation that distinguishes execution, quality, comparison, and repeatability claims

Use the results guide to interpret the dashboard and the readiness page to see current workload limitations.

title: Running Benchmarks
text: Three terms describe the core selection. A suite is a workload domain such as language or vision. A workload is one benchmark ID. A profile sets the contract depth. Modes, phases, devices, and experiment plans refine a selection only when the workload or study needs them.

title: Running Benchmarks
text:
Profiles








Profile
Meaning
Use it for




min
Fast functional path
Install check, smoke test, classroom demo, CI


max
Authoritative quality contract
Validated assignments, artifact review, baseline candidates


pro
Research envelope with controlled variants and knobs
Architecture, backend, quantization, and serving studies



min checks that a path runs, max exercises the candidate benchmark scale, and pro opens the research space. Results from min are smoke signals, not scores. A max result is comparable only when the workload quality contract, release validation, and public asset policy all pass.
A profile defines contract depth rather than a universal machine size. Every min and max path runs on local hardware. The MiniGo max path runs through a PyTorch adapter over the pinned upstream reference, at a self-play budget far below the reference contract, so it executes locally but does not yet make a quality claim.

title: Running Benchmarks
text:
Scenario Labels
Training and inference are execution modes under one workload identity. Inference may expose full, prefill, and decode phases. Scenario labels describe how requests are issued, while precision, compilation, quantization, batching, and scheduling remain reportable configurations rather than workload IDs.

title: Running Benchmarks
text:
Selecting What Runs
A bare --profile selects that profile’s default collection. The min default is the compact starter collection, max covers every registered workload, and pro selects the research collection. Use --collection all to run every workload at min or pro. The coverage validation preset runs every registered min path. --suite narrows to one domain, --workload selects one benchmark, and --mode or --phase selects an execution boundary when the workload exposes one. mlperf list --profile PROFILE always shows the current resolved selection.
uv run mlperf run --profile min                      # four-workload starter path
uv run mlperf run --profile min --collection all     # every min path
uv run mlperf run --suite vision --profile max       # one suite
uv run mlperf run --workload causal-language-modeling --profile max --mode training
uv run mlperf run --workload causal-language-modeling --profile max \
    --mode inference --phase decode
Add --dry-run to any of these to print the selection without running it. Each benchmark page lists its supported modes, phases, profiles, and controlled research configurations.






Warning



Select one workload for the first max run. A bare --profile max selects the full portfolio, which includes long downloads, expensive evaluations, and two environment-gated paths. Begin with image classification from the getting started guide.

title: Running Benchmarks
text:
Versioned Research Plans
A pro experiment plan turns a research question into a reviewable input artifact. It declares the conditions, controlled settings, device policy, outer-run count, power policy, and output location. The default remains one outer run per condition for initial quality and workflow review.
uv run mlperf run --plan examples/research/pro-collection/plan.yaml --dry-run
uv run mlperf run --plan examples/research/pro-collection/plan.yaml
--plan replaces --suite, --workload, --collection, --variant, --mode, and --phase. A CLI --device can override the plan for every condition, and --output-dir can redirect artifacts without editing the plan. Every condition receives a separate run directory. The suite aggregate records the normalized plan, its source SHA-256, the executed conditions, result fingerprints, and any CLI overrides.
A run can declare a baseline, candidate, or neutral condition role. Each workload, variant, mode, and phase comparison group can have at most one baseline, and every candidate group must have one. This lets a suite plan carry separate baselines for multiple benchmarks. When compatible throughput metrics exist, the dashboard shows candidate deltas against the matching baseline as descriptive evidence. The report still states that one outer run is not a stability result.
Plan environment settings are restricted to nonsensitive MLPERF_EDU_* configuration fields. Device and outer repetitions use dedicated fields. This keeps secrets out of result artifacts and makes configuration typos fail before execution.

title: Running Benchmarks
text:
Fetch Before You Measure
uv run mlperf fetch --workload image-classification --profile max
uv run mlperf fetch --profile max --dry-run     # preview all downloads
fetch downloads supported datasets and model weights, verifies available hash evidence, and populates the cache so the measured run contains no network time. A source checkout uses its existing data/ directory; an installed wheel uses the operating system’s per-user cache instead of the notebook’s current directory. Set MLPERF_EDU_DATA_DIR when a course needs a shared or preloaded location. mlperf doctor prints the resolved path, and uv run mlperf cache list shows what is on disk.

title: Running Benchmarks
text:
Long Runs and Recovery
The CLI does not yet provide a general run --resume option. Some workload-specific or legacy runners preserve intermediate state, but users should not assume that a partially completed suite run can resume. Before a long run, fetch assets, use doctor for the selected workload and profile, run with an explicit output directory, and review the workload page for its current recovery boundary.
See troubleshooting for interruption, cache, device, and provenance recovery. The local execution plan tracks suite-wide resume behavior as unfinished implementation work.

title: Running Benchmarks
text:
Blocked Local Max Runs
MiniGo currently fails closed on an ordinary classroom laptop, but its legacy setup is machine-readable. Ask doctor for the handoff when reviewing the existing reference path.
uv run mlperf doctor --workload reinforcement-learning --profile max --format json
The failing workload check includes a mlperf-edu-environment-handoff/0.1 object. The MiniGo handoff declares the NVIDIA GPU interface, immutable container digest, four-game review gate, pinned source files, workload-specific resumable execution, and final run command. A handoff documents the reference path. It is not a quality result and does not satisfy the local-execution milestone.
Recommendation used to appear here. Its contract moved from DLRM on Criteo Terabyte to MLPerf Training v0.5 NCF on MovieLens-20M, which trains locally, so it now runs the ordinary max path.
Maintainers can independently compare the three converted MLPerf Tiny PyTorch graphs with the pinned TFLite models over their complete official accuracy sets. The command is strict: any top-1 disagreement returns a nonzero status even when both executions pass the inherited quality target.
The committed three-resolver audit classifies the KWS PyTorch conversion as quality-preserving but nonidentical. The adapter remains available for inspectable educational runs, while promotion stays blocked until an exact-source path or authoritative unquantized weights establish exact parity. This decision does not create a disagreement tolerance.
uv run --extra parity python tools/audit_tflite_adapter_parity.py \
  --resolver auto --resolver builtin \
  --output /tmp/mlperf-edu-tflite-adapter-parity.json

title: Running Benchmarks
text:
Reports and Output
Runs write JSON, HTML, and CSV reports plus a .provd.json provenance artifact. Use --output-dir to choose the destination. The HTML dashboard opens by request only; pass --open-report when you want it shown immediately. Reports include a lead quality card, exact configuration, normalized training-checkpoint-inference lineage, hardware and software fingerprints, dataset and model dossiers, and quality-target status. The results guide covers how to read, verify, and package them.

title: Running Benchmarks
text:
Power Telemetry
uv run mlperf run --workload keyword-spotting --profile max --power
--power adds aggregate estimated watts and joules to the report using powermetrics on macOS or nvidia-smi on CUDA machines, without requiring privileged hardware counters. Treat the numbers as coarse energy telemetry for systems reasoning, not as calibrated power measurements.

title: Running Benchmarks
text:
Reproducibility Basics
Runs declare seeds and deterministic dataset recipes where their registry contracts require them. For candidate comparisons across machines, use --profile max, publish the generated fingerprint block unmodified, and keep the .provd.json artifact with the result. Score-bearing candidates must also pass the quality target and evidence protocol declared on their benchmark page.

title: Benchmark Registry

Warning



Independent preview. MLPerf EDU is not an official MLCommons benchmark and is not endorsed by MLCommons. Registry result labels are candidate classifications for review, not accepted MLPerf result categories.

The target is the MLPerf Training v0.5 recommendation quality target of 0.635 HR@10 for Neural Collaborative Filtering on MovieLens-20M. It is inherited, not project-created.
MLPerf retired the NCF recommendation benchmark after v0.5 because MovieLens-20M was too small to differentiate datacenter-scale systems. That property is what makes it appropriate here, and it is the same historical-MLPerf basis on which MiniGo is retained as the reinforcement-learning identity.
This replaces the DLRM and Criteo Terabyte contract, which could not execute inside the declared laptop envelope. That contract required manually licensed 1 TB data, a roughly 90 GB checkpoint, and a 256 GB-class runtime.

The parameter count is dominated by the user and item embedding tables and is left unverified until the runner constructs the model and reports it. Do not publish an estimated count.
{‘HR@10 is evaluated leave-one-out against 999 sampled negatives per user, for 1000 candidates per user. The count is part of the metric, not a tuning knob’: ‘re-scoring one trained checkpoint at 100 negatives gives 0.9336 and at 999 gives 0.5474, so a smaller candidate set makes the published target trivially beatable. An initial draft of this contract used 100, the convention from the original NCF paper on smaller datasets, and produced an implausible first-epoch pass. A held-out-item leakage check over 500 sampled users found 0 contaminated users, confirming the split itself is sound and the candidate count was the sole cause.’}
